text:
aj: quick heads-up — ran a long tail perf sweep on staging this morning. saw multiple small OOMs hitting the kv cache when a flurry of 1024-2048 token requests came through. not a gigantic spike, but consistent at ~27GB used on a 32GB slot.
maria: hmm, was that correlated with a kernel change? which commit on the runner image?
aj: nope, kernel selection stayed the same. the new change was the recent continuous-batcher tweak that tries to pack a few extra short requests into a window. suspect batches growing without checking per-kv-segment headroom.
devon: I pulled a flamegraph and allocation timeline. key signal: KV writeback + prefix pin spikes for ~200ms during those windows. attachment: https://internal.devops/graphs/231555/kv-spike.png
kai: thought: add an "early shepherd" admission path that rejects (soft-sheds) additions to an in-flight batch if estimated kv pressure margin < token_budget_margin. basically compute an expected KV footprint per token based on model+quantization and current kv fragmentation.
aj: exactly. sketch of the math I used in a quick repro:
```
kv_headroom = kv_capacity - current_kv_usage - safety_reserve_bytes
avg_kv_bytes_per_token = model_profile.kv_avg_bytes[token_len_bucket]
max_tokens_allowed = floor(kv_headroom / avg_kv_bytes_per_token)
if incoming_batch.tokens + inflight_batch.tokens > max_tokens_allowed: reject_or_shrink_new_request()
```
kai: couple notes: 1) safety_reserve_bytes should be dynamic (e.g., 5% of capacity or 1GB floor), 2) we should prefer shrinking the new request rather than rejecting when it's a multi-message job that can be truncated. also consider bucketized budgets per-kv-page-range — avoids global overconservative cuts.
maria: any perf cost for computing these estimates on admission path? we need it cheap (few ns ops). want to avoid telemetry-driven slowdowns.
devon: we can precalc avg_kv_bytes_per_token per model and per quant table during model load and keep a tiny histogram in shared memory. admission just a few integer ops + a memread — cheap.
aj: ran a quick AB test: enabling early-shepherd reduced the number of kv-related OOM restarts by 89% in staging and latency p99 for affected requests improved ~120ms (less kernel-level thrashing). throughput loss negligible (~0.4%).
kai: question: how does this interact with kernel selection? if a kernel switch increases per-token kv bytes (e.g., different kv layout), admission calc must consult the selected kernel's profile. we should tag model+kernel combo with a profile id.
aj: agreed — plan: profile per (model, kernel, quant) combo and store a compact tuple in model metadata. admission will load that id from the request routing info.
infra-bot: deploy: enabling kv-early-shepherd v1 to staging cluster redwood-stg-3 at 2026-03-18T09:42:00Z by aj :rocket:
maria: next steps: add canary flags to toggle behavior per-pool, add metrics (rejections, shrink_count, estimated_vs_actual_kv_bytes), and write an e2e with synthetic bursts.
devon: I'll add a lightweight end-to-end test that fuzzes request sizes and simulates fragmented kv pages. will push a draft PR today.
aj: action items: devon -> e2e test, kai -> refine bucketized headroom impl, maria -> metrics + canary flag, aj -> prod rollout plan and runbook. thanks all, this feels like a safe mitigation without heavy kernel surgery.
